title: The things that are not loot
summary: Not everything that looks worth carrying in R.E.P.O. is a valuable: the game keeps a separate kind of object with its own health and durability, and a valuable can even hide behind a prop that switches it in.
body: Not everything in a level that looks worth carrying is loot. The game keeps a kind of object that is explicitly not a valuable, and it is built to be broken rather than sold.
That object has presets of its own: a physical preset, an audio preset and a durability preset. Keeping the three apart is how the same object can be heavy in one level and fragile in another.
It can have health. There is a flag for whether it has any, a maximum, and a value at which it is considered destroyed, so an object can be worn down rather than only broken in one hit.

Breaking it costs health in three tiers: light, medium and heavy. That is the difference between a plate falling over and a shelf being driven into, and it is decided by the object rather than by the thing that hit it.
It has particle colours and its audio preset has a pitch, so what it sounds and looks like when it breaks is configured rather than borrowed from something else.

A valuable can be hidden behind a prop. There is a switch that holds a valuable and a prop together, with a parent for each and a name for the child, and a debug switch for testing it, which is how a valuable can be revealed rather than simply placed.

Some valuables move. There is one that copies a mesh, starts from a position, spins at an angular velocity, lasts a set time and then adds its value to the count — which is why catching it is a matter of timing.
Finding a valuable can be customised too. There is a discovery object with a wait before the tracker picks it up, corner and middle colours, and options for its own sound and its own map marker.
What this entry does not tell you: how much health any object has, what the break tiers cost, or how long an appearing valuable lasts. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: There is a kind of object that is explicitly not a valuable.
It has a physical, an audio and a durability preset of its own.
It can have health, with a maximum and a value at which it is destroyed.
Breaking it costs health in light, medium and heavy tiers.
It has particle colours and its audio preset has a pitch.
A valuable can be hidden behind a prop, with a parent for each, a name for the child and a debug switch.
facts.evidence: identifiers: ValuablePropSwitch, ValuableParent, PropParent, ChildValuableString, DebugSwitch

facts.claim: One valuable copies a mesh, starts at a position, spins at an angular velocity, lasts a set time and adds value.
facts.evidence: identifiers: AbsorbingValuable, meshCopy, startPosition, angularVelocity, effectiveDuration, timer, valueToAdd

facts.claim: Discovery can be customised with a wait time, corner and middle colours, and its own sound and map.
facts.evidence: identifiers: ValuableDiscoverCustom, waitTime, colorCorner, colorMiddle, hasCustomSound, customSound, hasCustomMap, customMap

facts.claim: The build names pieces of a level that are not loot at all, a storage-room door and a wet-floor sign among them, each with a texture of its own.
facts.evidence: asset names: Door Shop Storage Texture, Wet Floor Sign Albedo

alt.en: One of the level's own fittings, and not loot: the grey steel door of a storage room, lettered Storage.
alt.zh: 关卡自带的固定物、并非战利品：灰钢色的储藏室门，门上写着 Storage。

alt.en: Another fitting that is not loot: a yellow folding sign reading Caution, Wet Floor beside a slipping figure.
alt.zh: 另一件并非战利品的固定物：黄色折叠警示牌，写着 Caution, Wet Floor，旁边是滑倒的小人图案。

alt.en: Diagram: an object can be breakable rather than sellable, a valuable can hide behind a prop, and a discovered valuable can be marked with its own colours and sound.
alt.zh: 示意图：物件可以是可破坏物而非战利品；珍贵物可藏在道具后；被发现时有专属配色与音效。
